assumptions: THIS INCREMENT (job half, 2026-10-19): src/modules/platform-kernel/domain/jobs/ (CTR-JOB-001 record and checker; the job decisions as pure functions of a record, a supplied instant and the limits; the D6 provisional limits in job-limits.ts; the job stable errors) and application/jobs/ (JobStorePort, its in-memory fake with a manual clock, the workOnce worker step), with their tests; the manifest's outputs.files and two appended open_blockers. The outbox half (domain/outbox/, application/outbox/) is not in it.

The decisions read only CTR-JOB-001's timestamps and counters (app.jobs has no status column; the contract's freeze_boundary reserves lifecycle state names). The refusal and outcome names in code ('leased', 'exhausted', 'retry', 'dead_letter', ...) are internal, A0's inference, and never written to a record; dead-lettered is a predicate (attempt >= max_attempts, no result, no cancellation, no live lease), as 050's header reads it.

Every number in D6_PROVISIONAL_JOB_LIMITS (lease grace 30 s, heartbeat 60 s, back-off base 30 s, factor 2, cap 3600 s) is a test value, A0's inference; the decisions take the limits as a parameter. The lease runs timeout_seconds plus the grace from the claim; the claim order (higher priority, then earlier available_at) and retrying every failure while budget remains are A0's inferences, marked in code.

A job's tenant context is the minted context of the request that enqueued it (isMintedTenantContext); lookups, cancellation and every leased act are matched on the workspace as well as the job id. Enqueue with an existing (workspace_id, dedupe_key) returns the existing job (050's jobs_dedupe_key_unique), whatever its job_type or input_ref.

security_privacy_cost_impact: No provider, credential, network, data or cost. Security-relevant by design: a job carries only a minted tenant context and is never read, changed or leased across workspaces; a failure records a minted stable error's code only, never a thrown or returned value's text; a lease is fenced by attempt, so a reclaimed job cannot be overwritten by its earlier worker; handler lookup is by own property. A1 reads it (risk lane).
migration_and_data_impact: None: no migration, no db/** change; the code is not wired to app.jobs (the adapter is scope.exclude).
compatibility_impact: Additive: new files under domain/jobs/ and application/jobs/ only; nothing imports them yet (index.ts and run.ts unchanged). No contract-catalog, dependency or tool-configuration change.
known_limitations: The outbox half (CTR-EVT-001 checker, relay port, replay-safe consumer; criteria 2 (event half) and 5) is not written; it is the next increment on this branch.

The D6 limits are test values; the per-round budget and concurrency are not modelled (the dispatcher increment). The worker bounds a handler by the job clock's waitUntil; a real timer is the adapter's.

The fake's claim is atomic because each method completes synchronously; the database adapter's equivalent (a single-statement claim) is scope.exclude, so criterion 4's 'at most one lease' is shown on the fake only.
